title: Three small fires in the mist

events.text: I am painting three rosehips on an arching twig against cool mist. Goal: long joined warm planes and one compact light on the nearest hip. Inspiration: https://www.nps.gov/romo/rose_hips.htm
Four broad planes left linen lanes. Wet overlapping bridges will join the mist before the twig.
The wet bridges closed the linen lanes, leaving soft bands. I will set one rising branch and three unequal fruit positions.
The branch reads clearly but the right fork is detached. First I will build the large left hip as a filled warm mass.
The first hip is solid with no hollow; its right turn is dark and ridged. I will make the right hip smaller and more red.
The right hip is filled, but the fork repair widened its loose end. I will bridge farther back and place the small upper hip.
Three unequal warm masses now balance the branch. The right fork still misses by a narrow strip; a short crossing join will fix its attachment.
The fork is finally attached, with a thick stepped joint. The first leaf is banana-shaped; a broad inner plane can give it a fuller blade.
The leaves remain narrow ribbons. I will fill their lower bellies and taper their ends instead of tracing another outline.
Filled bellies made the leaves broader; the right still has a blunt tip. The tiny dark crown gives the nearest hip a dried flower end.
The sepals are small and unequal. I will complete the upper crown and add warm planes to strengthen the fruit volume.
Warm shoulder planes stayed inside the silhouettes. The near hip has a hard dark crescent; a middle red will soften that transition.
The middle red softened the near crescent partly; the upper hip now has a narrow dark seam. I will warm that seam and add tapered leaf tips.
The leaf-tip additions barely changed the blunt ends, and the fine vein stays quiet. I will interrupt the mist bands with long wet verticals in open space.
The wet verticals changed the bands only subtly. I will add a few unequal thorns and a broken warm branch edge, keeping the mist open.
Sparse thorns taper into the air. I will test one short warm light on the nearest shoulder by itself.
The single light stays compact but subdued. I will support it with warm surrounding color, and give the leaves quieter interior veins.
I am leaning upward to check the complete calyces and the small hip. The central close view crops these edges.
The upper pan shows complete joined crowns and a contained light; regular oil ridges remain. I will break the left leaf edge with a few tapered teeth.
Those small strokes landed inside the leaf and read as veins, not teeth. I will place the next tips clearly beyond the silhouette.
The external teeth became hooks and crosswise bars. I will absorb their roots into broad leaf planes, retaining only small irregular tips.
Broad low-body covers only partly absorbed the leaf bars. I will test loaded matched color and unify the stepped fork into one collar.
Loaded paint unified the fork collar more clearly, while leaf relief remained. I will add sparse skin folds near the fruit bases, keeping them darker than the light.
The near skin fold is a hard short slash; the right fold is quieter. I will soften the near slash and warm the fruit-to-stem attachments.
The matched warm cover removed most of the near slash. Attachments are joined. I will soften the bare branch tip so it does not compete with the dried crowns.
Mist paint barely softened the twig tip; the regular relief persists. I will give the crowns a few dry warm edges without adding another bright fruit light.
The dry crown edges remain subtle. The fruit are still joined; I will strengthen a few lower turns with middle values rather than dark outlines.
Middle-value turns kept the fruit solid, with some raised lower patches. I will close exposed top linen and vary open mist near the bottom.
The top linen strip is covered; the mist retains soft bands. Final refinement: join each dried crown into its fruit shoulder with muted rust.
The crown joins made narrow warm rings. I will absorb their lower edges with broader fruit planes and stop before the light or silhouettes spread.

Finished at 112 completed marks. Long overlaps joined three unequal hips, the loaded fork repair connected its collar, and the near light stayed compact. Leaf teeth became hooks; covers only partly softened relief. Crown rings and mist bands remain. I am stopping before further covers enlarge those patches.

creation.goal: Join rounded rosehips with long warm planes and reserve one compact light on the nearest hip.

inspiration.description: Original imagined three rosehips on an arching thorny twig against cool mist, sparked by the NPS Rocky Mountain rosehip guide. No finished composition copied.

creation.workflow: 112 animated completed strokes in batches of 1–4; 31 live text notes, 90 moments. Each next batch composed after paired screenshot inspection. Deliberate crown refinement108–112, then repeated final pair.
creation.inspectionEvidence: 29 distinct completed-stroke boundaries inspected as settled whole and 2.0x close pairs, including isolated light61; repeated final112 pair and direct upper pan64. All pairs saved with unique explicit filenames. Whole views show the complete canvas; default close crops crowns, upper pan includes complete calyces. Camera badges confirmed after settling; batches waited for animation and completed count. Actual 900x620 browser PNG visually inspected.
creation.notes: All easel text and camera moments recorded live. Provenance and assessment appended after browser PNG and JSON exports. Previous browser PNG and replay preserved before clear.
